sources.title: Government of The Gambia: Immigration and Visa Information
sources.officialityEvidence: This live entry guidance is published on the Government of The Gambia’s gambia.gov.gm domain, identifies the official immigration information page, and links readers to Gambia Immigration Department visa information.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the United Kingdom, full members of the European Union, the Commonwealth [and] ECOWAS do not require a visa.

sources.title: Gambia Immigration Department: Visa services and country table
sources.officialityEvidence: GID publishes this live visa page on its official gid.gov.gm domain. Its associated WordPress endpoint reported modification on 31 October 2025; the page names exemption, visa, clearance, and visa-and-clearance groups.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ECOWAS Member States Allows Free Entry

sources.title: Gambia Immigration Department: Entry requirements
sources.officialityEvidence: The official GID site publishes this current entry-requirements page, including visa, entry-clearance, travel-document, screening, and port-of-entry guidance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Currently, the visa system in the Gambia is a sticker and by endorsement.

sources.title: Government of The Gambia: Passport Office
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Government Passport Office page identifies the Immigration Act authority, describes ordinary passports, and directly describes emergency passport travel back to The Gambia for a Gambian citizen.
sources.supportingExcerpt: shall issue him or her Emergency Passport to travel back to the Gambia.

sources.title: EUR-Lex: Member States
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex is the European Union’s official legal-information portal. The live Member States page enumerates the current 27 EU members, including Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Now there are 27 Member States: Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland.

policies.title: Gambian ordinary passport: citizenship/home entry
policies.summary: The Government’s Passport Office directly describes a Gambian citizen obtaining an emergency passport to travel back to The Gambia. This supports only the ordinary-passport citizenship/home normalization.
conditions: This normalizes the Gambian ordinary-passport home/citizenship cell, not residence, former citizenship, nationality disputes, diplomatic, service, official, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special-document treatment.

The cited page’s direct return example concerns loss or destitution and an emergency passport. Identity, document validity, health, security, screening and other lawful border controls remain applicable.

policies.title: Reconciled named ordinary passports: visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The current GID table expressly lists 11 ECOWAS passports with free entry and 18 visa-exemption agreements; Indonesia is excluded because the same table also places it in a clearance group. The central Government page, read with the current EU membership list, additionally supports Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia because GID supplies no contrary row for them. This produces 32 supported foreign ordinary-passport exemptions.
conditions: GID’s named ECOWAS and visa-exemption-agreement groups directly support the listed foreign passports. Indonesia is deliberately not included: the same GID table also lists it as needing clearance.

Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia are retained solely because the Government’s current EU waiver statement expressly covers full EU members and the current GID table supplies no contrary country row for those four passports.

The Government page frames the waiver as holiday or business travel not exceeding 90 days. The GID table itself does not publish an exemption-specific stay period; valid travel documents, yellow-fever evidence where applicable, funds/onward travel, entry conditions, security screening and final admission remain applicable.

This is an ordinary nationality-passport baseline only; it does not establish treatment for British Overseas Territories, Crown Dependencies, Hong Kong, Macao, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency, residence or other special documents.

No electronic visa is normalized: GID says the visa system is sticker and endorsement. The generic statement that a visa may be obtained at a gazetted port does not identify an arrival-issuance cohort for any additional nationality.
